title: 1M: Execute Dayli ICC
hook: Is the entry model actually present? Then, and only then, you act.

launchpad.outcome: Mark the PIL, confirm Indication, Correction and Continuation with closes, plan the limit entry at the retest, and spot a setup you must skip.
launchpad.missionQuestion: Is the entry model actually present?

slides.headline: Is the entry model actually present? Then you act.
slides.line: This is where your plan meets the 1-minute chart. You act only when price completes every step of Dayli ICC.

slides.headline: Finish your higher timeframe work before you open the 1M.
slides.line: HTF means higher timeframe. The 1M doesn’t create the whole trade idea, so it always comes last.

cards.label: 4H: read the room
cards.sub: The range, the structure, and the current ICC chapter.

cards.label: 1H: build the map
cards.sub: The relevant swings and levels price is trading around.

cards.label: 15M: the checkpoint
cards.sub: Recommended for extra confluence, but not required.

slides.headline: Mark your PIL before you look for the sequence.
slides.line: The PIL, or Pre-Indication Level, is the swing price has to prove itself through. You choose it by structural relevance, exactly as Section 13 taught.

steps.text: Price made a swing high, then pulled back below it.
That swing high is the PIL. To resume upward, price has to prove itself through it. No PIL, no valid indication.

slides.headline: Indication is a 1M candle that closes through the PIL.
slides.line: Bullish means a 1M candle closes above the PIL. Bearish means a 1M candle closes below it.

steps.text: Indication: this 1M candle closed above the PIL. Price proved it with the close.

check.prompt: A 1M candle’s wick pokes above the PIL, but the candle closes below it. Is that indication?

options.label: Yes, price went above the level
options.feedback: The wick only shows where price traveled. Indication needs the 1M candle to close above the PIL.

options.label: No, a wick alone doesn’t count
options.why: Right. Wicks don’t vote. Price visiting the level proves nothing until a candle closes through it.

slides.headline: Correction is a candle that closes back through the PIL.
slides.line: After a bullish indication, the correction is a close back below the PIL. It is part of the model, not a failure.

steps.text: Correction: this candle closed back below the PIL. The correction is complete.

check.prompt: After indication, price stalls just above the PIL for three candles but never closes below it. Is that a correction?

options.label: Yes, price is clearly pulling back
options.feedback: Price is only hesitating. A correction needs a candle to close back below the PIL, and we don’t invent the correction.

options.label: No, nothing has closed back below yet
options.why: Exactly. Hesitating is not correcting. You wait for the close back through the PIL.

slides.headline: Continuation closes back through the PIL in the original direction.
slides.line: For a bullish setup, that is a close back above the PIL. Now all three stages are complete.

steps.text: Continuation: this candle closed back above the PIL. Indication, Correction, Continuation: the sequence is complete.

slides.headline: A complete ICC doesn’t guarantee an entry.
slides.line: Tap each step. Your planned limit entry sits at the PIL, and it only fills if price comes back to it.

steps.label: I · Indication
steps.sub: A 1M candle closes through the PIL.

steps.label: C · Correction
steps.sub: A candle closes back through the PIL.

steps.label: C · Continuation
steps.sub: A candle closes back through in the original direction.

steps.label: Wait for the retest
steps.sub: Price has to come back to the PIL. You do nothing until it does.

steps.label: Limit entry at the PIL
steps.sub: Your planned entry is the PIL price, not wherever price is now.

slides.headline: In the MNQ example, the stop is 30 points and the target 60.
slides.line: You risk 30 points to make 60, so the risk-to-reward is 1:2. These numbers are an example from the Dayli ICC MNQ framework, not a rule for every product or account.

steps.text: Stop loss: 30 points below the entry. MNQ moves $2 per point per contract, so that is $60 of risk on 1 contract.
Take profit: 60 points above the entry. That is $120 on 1 contract, twice what you risked.

check.prompt: Same plan, but you trade 2 MNQ contracts instead of 1. What are the risk and the reward?

options.label: $60 risk and $120 reward
options.feedback: That is 1 contract. The points stay the same, but every extra contract adds the same dollar exposure again.

options.label: $120 risk and $240 reward
options.why: Right. 30 × $2 × 2 = $120 and 60 × $2 × 2 = $240. Points don’t move with size, but your dollar exposure does.

options.label: $240 risk and $480 reward
options.feedback: That would be 4 contracts. Multiply points by $2, then by the number of contracts.

slides.headline: After the sequence, wait for price to come back to you.
slides.line: If price returns to the PIL, your planned limit entry can be considered. If it never returns, that is a missed trade.

steps.text: Price runs away from the PIL. You don’t chase it. You wait.
Price comes back down to the PIL. That is the first retest.
Now your planned limit entry at the PIL can be considered. If price had gone to target without coming back, it would be a missed trade, not a bad trade.

slides.headline: Which setups are incomplete or invalid, and must be skipped?
slides.line: Tap each one. If any of these is true, there is no entry for you.

cards.label: Indication, no correction
cards.sub: Price closed through and never closed back. The sequence isn’t complete.

cards.label: Correction, no continuation
cards.sub: Price closed back but never closed through again in the original direction.

cards.label: Wick-only breaks
cards.sub: A wick through the PIL is a visit, not proof. Only closes count.

cards.label: Entry already missed
cards.sub: The retest came and went, or never came. Don’t chase.

cards.label: Against your thesis
cards.sub: An entry that conflicts with your planned structural thesis is skipped.

check.prompt: Price closed above the PIL, then closed back below, then only wicked back above it. Is the sequence complete?

options.label: Yes, all three steps happened
options.feedback: Wicks don’t complete anything. Continuation needs a candle to close back above the PIL.

options.label: No, continuation isn’t confirmed
options.why: Right. While the closes stay on the wrong side, continuation is not confirmed, so there is no entry.

slides.title: Mark every step, then take the entry.
slides.body: Read the HTF context first. Then mark the PIL and confirm each step only after a candle closes.

scenario.structure: Pullback from a 1M swing high. Price is below it.

candidates.label: A
candidates.why: The swing high this pullback came from. To resume upward, price has to prove itself through it.

candidates.label: B
candidates.why: That is the low of the pullback. A bullish sequence starts below the PIL and proves itself up through the swing high.

options.label: It’s structurally relevant to the current move
options.why: Exactly: it’s the swing the current pullback came from.

options.label: It’s the newest swing
options.feedback: Newest isn’t the test. Relevance is.

slides.intro: Tap the swing that is your PIL. Then press Play or Next candle, and confirm each step as price earns it.

end.card:
I · C · C → RETEST → ENTRY.
Price earned every step before you acted.

slides.title: The sequence completed. Does the entry ever come?

scenario.structure: Pullback from the swing high at the PIL. Price is below it.

slides.passWhy: MISSED TRADE ✓ The setup was valid, but price never came back to the PIL. You don’t chase, so you skip it.
slides.passMiss: Give price a chance to come back to the PIL first.
slides.intro: Indication, Correction and Continuation are already in. Place your planned limit entry, then watch what price does.

end.card:
A MISSED TRADE IS NOT A BAD TRADE.
It’s just a trade you didn’t get.

slides.title: Replay a bearish setup and check each requirement.
slides.body: Bearish mirrors bullish: close below, close back above, close back below, then the retest.

scenario.structure: Bounce into the swing low at the PIL. Price is above it.

options.label: No, nothing has closed below the PIL
options.why: Right. Bearish indication needs a 1M candle to close below the PIL.

options.label: Yes, price is close enough
options.feedback: Close enough isn’t a close. Wait for a candle to close below the PIL.

pauses.text: INDICATION ✓ This candle closed below the PIL.

ask.prompt: What does price need to do next?

options.label: Close back above the PIL
options.why: Yes. That close back above is the correction.

options.label: Keep falling so I can sell
options.feedback: Not yet. The model still needs a correction: a close back above the PIL.

pauses.text: CONTINUATION ✓ Closed below, back above, back below. The sequence is complete.

options.label: No, I wait for the retest of the PIL
options.why: Exactly. Your planned limit entry is at the PIL, so you wait for price to come back to you.

options.label: Yes, before it gets away
options.feedback: That’s chasing. Price moving without you doesn’t create a new rule. Your plan was the retest.

end.card:
SAME RULES, MIRRORED.
Has the next ICC requirement been satisfied? If not, wait.

slides.quote: Is the entry model actually present? Then, and only then, you act.

slides.prompt: In your own words, what has to happen before you place a 1M entry?
slides.modelAnswer: My 4H and 1H work is done, and the 15M if I use it. I mark the PIL first. Then a 1M candle closes through it (Indication), a candle closes back through it (Correction), and a candle closes through it again in the original direction (Continuation). Then I wait for price to retest the PIL, where my planned limit entry sits, with a defined stop and target like the 30-point stop and 60-point target in the MNQ example. If any step is missing, or the retest never comes, I skip it.

takeaways: Finish the 4H and 1H first, and mark the PIL before anything else.
Indication, Correction and Continuation all need candle closes through the PIL.
A complete ICC still needs the retest before the planned limit entry.
No retest, a wick-only break or a missing step means you skip it.
remember: NO COMPLETE MODEL, NO RETEST, NO ENTRY.
